_note: Targeted checks for AI reader 194: first-reader anchors from your sources that the blind reconciliation did not match.

tasks.locator: Methods › Recruitment and Randomization, 1st and 2nd paragraphs, and Assessment, 1st paragraph (p. 2004); Figure 1 (p. 2005); Treatment Conditions (p. 2006)
tasks.extracted: 1383 people with DSM-IV alcohol dependence, recruited by advertisements and clinical referrals at 11 US academic sites and abstinent for 4 to 21 days, were randomized to 9 groups: medical management (9 sessions with a health care professional) with naltrexone, acamprosate, both or two placebos, each with or without a combined behavioural intervention (CBI) delivered by specialists in up to twenty 50-minute sessions, or CBI alone without pills or medical management. People with other substance use disorders (except nicotine or cannabis) or psychiatric disorders requiring medication were excluded. The research assistants who assessed drinking were not blinded to psychosocial treatment.

tasks.locator: Results › Within-Treatment Drinking Outcomes for Pill-Taking Groups › Primary Outcomes, 2nd and 3rd paragraphs; Table 3 (p. 2009); Figure 2 (p. 2010)
tasks.extracted: Percent days abstinent during treatment, least-squares means: CBI 78.2 against no CBI 77.8 (P=.82); naltrexone × CBI interaction P=.009, with placebo and no CBI 75.1, naltrexone without CBI 80.6, CBI with placebo 79.2 and naltrexone with CBI 77.1 (pooled over acamprosate); the authors state that combined naltrexone and CBI showed no incremental benefit over CBI or naltrexone alone. Effect sizes (Cohen d, 97.5% CI): CBI main effect 0.01 (−0.12 to 0.14); against placebo naltrexone without CBI, naltrexone without CBI 0.22 (0.03 to 0.40), CBI without naltrexone 0.17 (−0.02 to 0.35), naltrexone with CBI 0.07 (−0.11 to 0.25). Time to the first heavy drinking day: CBI main-effect hazard ratio 0.81 (0.60 to 1.10); the paper does not say how its main-effect hazard ratios were coded, and by their intervals they may compare single groups rather than the whole factorial (a reporting issue on the study card).

The authors interpret the short palpebral fissures as secondary to deficient growth of the eyes (microphthalmia noted at birth in patients 1 and 7), the maxillary hypoplasia as producing relative prognathism, and the joint and palmar-crease changes as consequences of limited movement or aberrant position early in fetal life; of the five children with a cardiac anomaly, three were considered to have had a ventricular septal defect that closed before 1 year of age. The paragraph calls the pattern this syndrome; the paper nowhere uses the name fetal alcohol syndrome.
